I’ve learned to get nervous when somebody knows too much about me too soon. We’re twin flames. She knows my motives. I’m Lord Krishna. Okay, maybe I really am way better than the other guys she’s found. But if she hasn’t found anything about me that bothers her yet, she hasn’t found all of me.

I still love women I’ve loved before. Sometimes I talk about them because I’m thinking about them. I’m not trying to make her jealous. If she can’t handle that I still love them, she isn’t ready for me.

If she says, “Can you talk less about your exes?” Sure. Maybe I do talk about them too much sometimes. But they still matter to me. If I’m supposed to listen to everything on her mind, I don’t want to have to pretend that isn’t on mine.

Seeing somebody's highest potential can become another way of avoiding the actual person. I may see something in a woman before she fully lives it, but then I have to ask her:

“I see this in you, and I think it’s special. Do you wanna reach for it together?”

If she says no, forget it. You’re in la la land. If she says yes, ask what is blocking her. Is the block more than you can handle? Or does she mostly need somebody to join her on the journey and believe in her?

Partners should help each other grow. Who else is going to do it? Your mom and dad? You’re already grown. Everybody else will usually be a smaller influence, so you’d better choose someone who helps you grow well. Like the FM Laeti song here says, “Inspire her to see the best in herself, actualize that.” If something severe is happening, sometimes a demand or boundary is necessary too.

See whether the other person will stay in the conversation. If they won’t, that tells you something another perfectly worded speech probably won’t fix.

Usually one person wants to open this door before the other. If I'm the one asking for honesty, I have to be willing to hear that the relationship may need to change in a way I don't want. That's where the selfless kind of love from the beginning comes in. But the other person can't keep saying “not now” forever. After a while, refusing to choose is a choice.

## Outside help can sometimes break the loop fast

Bee and I were once desperately misunderstanding each other, so we called my friend Eshwar, the only friend of mine whom she respected. He told a related story about something that had happened with his sister. Somehow, Bee immediately understood what I had been trying to say. It was like magic.

If the eros does fade, maybe the agape is enough to keep us together. But *maybe* cuts both ways. If I tell her, “Even if I stop wanting you, I may still stay because I love you,” what exactly did I reassure her of? I may stay without wanting her. I may leave anyway. If she still wants me, both possibilities are awful.

Maybe some couples end up treasuring the life they built more than the desire that started it. Maybe staying without eros feels like settling, and neither person feels good about that. No one standing at the wedding can know which marriage theirs will become.

Why talk before sex? Because once we're already having it, an honest answer might interrupt the thing that has begun. Beforehand, the conversation can go wherever it needs to. Having it is already part of the difference between making love and merely having sex.

I would want to know what she desires and what helps her body feel safe. Are there kinks or particular dynamics that matter? What has her erotic history taught her? What has mine taught me? What reliably doesn't work? Is sex recreation, bonding, sacred practice, stress relief, or all of that? How often do we imagine wanting it? If one of us wants more, less, or something different—and over a long relationship, one of us probably will for a while—what do we do then? Mismatched desire is one of the great factories of quiet resentment.

Maybe we don't know yet. That's a real answer. *I don't know, but I'm willing to find out honestly with you* is better than assuming our bodies will negotiate everything for us.

To me, sexual compatibility is not only whether two bodies fit. It is whether two people can stay honest while they are maximally exposed. If we can talk this frankly before our clothes come off, we've already practiced some of the trust, attention, and willingness to be seen that making love requires.

Before sex, I want to know whether we can talk about sex. What do you actually desire? What helps your body feel safe? Are there kinks or dynamics that matter? What has your history taught you, and what reliably doesn't work? If you imagine sex as bonding or sacred practice and I imagine recreation or stress relief, that matters. So does how often each of us thinks we'll want it.

We may not know. Fine. *I don't know, but I'm willing to find out honestly with you* is a real answer. The point is not to finish the conversation in advance. It is to find out whether we can have it.

Most couples wait until they're already sleeping together. By then an honest answer might interrupt something that has started, so there are places the later conversation often can't go. Talking while either person can still say no is already part of the difference between making love and merely having sex.

Desire will probably become mismatched at some point in a long relationship. One person will want more, less, or something different for a while, and that mismatch is one of the great factories of quiet resentment. We can't solve it beforehand. We can find out whether we'll be able to speak when it happens.

For me, sexual compatibility is not only whether two bodies fit. It is whether two people can stay honest while they are maximally exposed. If we can do that before our clothes come off, we've already practiced some of the trust, attention, and willingness to be seen that making love requires.

“I don’t know whether I want something serious with you. I’m not pretending I do. I’d still like to have sex.”

That's honest about what you want right now. It still leaves the larger question untouched: what do you owe each other if sex creates something neither of you expected? Sex can make a child. If this girl gets pregnant, she’s gonna call you. Then what? You block her? Agree to child support? Try to convince her to abort when she thinks abortion is killing her child? This is what penetrative sex can do. No contraception is perfect.
